subject: Request: Bespoke commissioning credit + packaging exception for Astera Health (VP/CFO sign-off)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Bespoke commissioning credit + packaging exception for Astera Health (VP/CFO sign-off)

Team —

Quick summary: Astera Health (strategic prospect in cardiology vertical) is asking us to include a one-time commissioning credit and waive the onboarding packaging surcharge for their Dedicated deployment. Key commercial asks from procurement: 30% one-time commissioning credit (applied to first invoice) + waiver of $25k packaging surcharge. In return they will sign a 12‑month committed run-rate of ~$350k/month (multiregion) and agree to an annual review clause. HubSpot: DL-2026-1034.

Why this needs VP/CFO signoff: this is outside our standard guardrails (one-time credits normally capped at 15% for this segment; packaging surcharge waiver requires exec signoff given hardware footprints). Finance has modeled the unit economics and we need explicit VP/CFO authorization to proceed.

Ask: can we get a signoff or a short memo I can send to Lara so legal/procurement can proceed with DocuSign this week? I attached the latest commissioning plan and cost breakdown.

Context / constraints (short):
- Customer is asking for committed capacity on Dedicated (pinned model variants).
- They commit to a twelve-month, $4.2M ARR (approx).
- We estimate $0.6M incremental cost in onboarding/headroom in Q1 if we waive the surcharge and provide the credit.
- Suggested mitigations: staggered invoicing for the credit (50/50 across first two invoices), explicit surge protection cap, and a rollback clause if usage underperforms the committed run-rate by >40% after month 3.

Attachments: Astera_MA_plan_v2.pdf (commercial summary) and commissioning-cost-breakdown.xlsx (ops model).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Bespoke commissioning credit + packaging exception for Astera Health (VP/CFO sign-off)

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. I ran a quick commercial ops model and annotated the commissioning-cost-breakdown.xlsx with the margin impact and risk gates. Short take: financially palatable if we (A) split the credit across the first two invoices (reduces Q1 P&L hit by roughly 50%), (B) keep the packaging surcharge waived only if they commit to capacity + a short runway for accelerated payment if usage ramps >120% of committed, and (C) require a usage true-up clause at month 3.

My recommendation (for VP/CFO): approve the 30% one-time commissioning credit on the condition that we:
- Apply 50% on invoice 1 and 50% on invoice 2;
- Include a surge cap (max 150% of committed baseline before auto-rate adjustment);
- Keep packaging surcharge waived but only for the initial deployment cluster (region us-west) — any cross-region expansions will reinstate packaging charges;
- Finance to monitor monthly for 90 days and reserve right to invoice a retrospective adjustment if committed floors not met.

I attached the annotated spreadsheet and included a short one-paragraph memo below you can paste to the VP/CFO: 

"Commercial ops endorses a 30% one-time commissioning credit (split across two invoices) and a one-time packaging surcharge waiver for Astera Health contingent on a 12-month committed run-rate (~$350k/month). Mitigation: surge cap and a 90-day true-up clause. Estimated incremental Q1 cost to Redwood ~ $600k. Approval required due to packaging waiver and credit magnitude"

If Marcus is OK with that language, I think it's ready to route to VP/CFO for signoff.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: commissioning-cost-breakdown-annotated.xlsx (see tab "risk_gates")

+1 to Kimberly's approach. Astera is strategic for our cardiology playbook and the topline ARR opportunity justifies a temporary concession if we lock the commitment and contractually enforce the mitigations. Two small asks before I push to the execs:

1) Can legal add explicit termination/true-up language that allows us to claw back the credit pro rata if they under-deliver against the committed baseline at month 3?
2) I want the one-paragraph memo to the VP/CFO to include an explicit ask: "Authorization for one-time exception to our packaging surcharge policy and approval for the 30% commissioning credit (split across invoices)" — helps expedite the finance approval routing.

If you can draft and paste that memo here, I'll forward to VP and cc CFO, copying legal.
